pure-announcement.rationale: This is a technical concepts guide explaining an isolation mechanism, not a launch or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: remocal-development covers process-level syscall interception joining a local process to one remote pod; this note covers request-level routing across a shared cluster via routing-key headers and context propagation — a distinct mechanism a remocal-development reader would not learn.

unfalsifiable.rationale: First-party technical documentation naming the concrete, checkable mechanism: routing-key headers, OpenTelemetry-based context propagation, and Istio/DevMesh-sidecar routing.

durability.rationale: Request routing plus header-based context propagation is a general architectural pattern for shared-cluster test isolation, independent of Signadot's pricing or feature roadmap.

actionability.rationale: A reader gets the two concrete primitives needed to build request-scoped isolation themselves — routing-key headers and OpenTelemetry context propagation — plus the real trade-off between service-mesh and sidecar-based routing.

atomicity.rationale: One idea throughout: how isolation is achieved for a request-scoped sandbox on a shared cluster; routing and propagation are two halves of that single mechanism, not separate topics.
